reason: Connect the retort to hydrogen so it can process the iron-rich feedstock.
expectation: I expect the retort to gain a controlled hydrogen supply for reducing iron minerals; it may still need feedstock and heat.

alternatives.reason: The cable and steel may be useful for equipment, but the retort connection seems more directly tied to the goal.

effect: The retort now has heat and controlled hydrogen, but still needs concentrate.
reaction: The contained exhaust and condensate make the setup feel thoughtfully engineered.
reason: This is the only available combination, so I'll use it to advance the setup.
expectation: I expect the cable and steel to make some powered workshop equipment, though its purpose is unclear.

effect: The powered coil is a separator for extracting magnetic grains from the screened regolith.
reaction: Switching off the magnet to release the grains is a satisfying practical detail.
reason: Use the only available combination to prepare feedstock for the retort.
expectation: I expect it to separate a magnetic, iron-rich fraction from the regolith, though further processing will be needed.

effect: The separator produced assayed iron-rich concentrate ready for the retort.
reaction: The distinction between red colour and an actual mineral assay is a useful detail.
reason: Feed the concentrate into the prepared retort; it's the only available combination and advances the iron goal.
expectation: I expect heat and hydrogen to reduce the iron-bearing minerals, though the resulting material may need further processing.

effect: The concentrate has been reduced to porous iron, which needs pressing into a more usable form.
reaction: The explanation of hydrogen removing oxygen makes the transformation clear.
reason: Press the iron sponge; it's the only available action and should advance the iron-making goal.
expectation: I expect the press to compact the porous iron into a denser form, though it may need further treatment.

effect: The heated press consolidated the sponge into a dense billet; the new goal is to shape it into a process frame.
reaction: The distinction between consolidating the iron and shaping parts makes the process clear.
reason: Use the only available combination to shape the billet for the process frame.
expectation: I expect the press to form the consolidated iron into a frame or frame components.

effect: The billet is now shaped into non-pressure supports ready for the return-plant footing.
reaction: The distinction between supports and flight hardware is reassuringly specific.
reason: Fit the bars and brackets to the footing to make the process frame; it's the only available combination.
expectation: I expect a stable frame for the return-fuel equipment, though it may need further fittings.

effect: The local iron supports now form a completed frame for the gas installation, completing the chapter's goals.
reaction: It's satisfying to see the processed material become a concrete part of the return plant.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reducing the concentrate with hydrogen was the strongest moment: it explained how oxygen is removed from the minerals and why the resulting iron still needs processing.

leastWorthwhile.text: Shaping and installing the supports felt fairly predictable, particularly with only one action offered at each step.

surprise.text: The electromagnet's purpose was initially unclear, but it became a practical way to separate iron-rich grains; the assay also showed why red colour alone isn't proof of suitable minerals.

arbitrary.text: The cable-and-steel combination initially lacked a clear purpose, though the resulting separator explained it. It was also the only available action at that point.

continue.text: Yes. I'd like to see how the locally made frame supports the return-fuel installation and how the discovery gets home; the processing details made this chapter worthwhile despite its mostly linear choices.
